clauses.reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12370 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 1 establishes, effective July 10, 1982, a three-member board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. No earlier express end was found.

Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12370 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 2 directs the board to report within 30 days from the date of its creation. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The board's report is dated August 19, 1982 (held report of Emergency Board No. 194; the time was extended from August 9 to August 19, 1982 with the President's approval on July 26, 1982), so the command was functionally spent on August 19, 1982; that date is stated here and not entered as a later event because no dossier evidence record covers the transmittal letter or the extension passage. No earlier express end was found.

Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12370 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Section 3 restates the section 10 status-quo period, from the date of creation of the board until 30 days after its report. The statutory standstill (status-quo period) is likewise a spent fact and not an end; it ran until thirty days after the report dated August 19, 1982, that is to about September 18, 1982 (a computed date, not shown in a source). No earlier express end was found.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12370 (47 FR 30047, Federal Register of July 12, 1982; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute Between the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Certain Railroads Represented by the National Carriers’ Conference Committee of the National Railway Labor Conference and signed July 8, 1982. It creates a board to investigate the dispute between the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and certain railroads represented by the National Carriers’ Conference Committee of the National Railway Labor Conference. Inventory: the order is a board order whose operative commands are 3 clause(s) as recorded in the dossier (sec1; sec2; sec3). The list of parties attached to the order identifies the dispute and is not a separate command. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12370 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C): the report date and the end of any statutory standstill are spent facts that do not end the order; the held report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_12370_Report_of_Presidential_Emergency_Board_No._194_created_by_EO_12370_effective_July_10__6dbdcaaa92.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) shows that the board's report and recommendations were submitted to the President by a letter of transmittal dated August 19, 1982 (the cover is also dated August 19, 1982), after the President approved on July 26, 1982 an extension of the time for the report from August 9, 1982 to August 19, 1982. The board therefore made its report on August 19, 1982, the report command was functionally spent on that date, and the thirty-day period after the report ran to about September 18, 1982 (a computed date, thirty days after the transmittal date, not a date shown in the source). These dates are stated here and not entered as later events because no dossier evidence record covers the transmittal letter or the extension passage (the dossier's records from that file quote other passages of the report). The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found citations of this number outside its own printings only in an emergency-board report held under jobs/source-ladder. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).
